complexity_ledger.narrative: CM-01 fixed CM-F1 and mechanized the case-module declaration and coverage report. The defect was real and reproduced exactly as briefed: on the shipped three-module example the ledger measured Core.tla against External.cfg and recorded variables 0, actions 0, bound None, modularity 0.0 -- for a module with no variables and no actions. It now measures External.tla + External.cfg and records variables 10, actions 12, modularity 0.047 (results/cm-f1-model-discovery.txt). Model discovery is declared first (manifest `model:`), then the outermost view of a Core/Internal/External baseline, then a legacy single module; an unresolvable directory and a .tla/.cfg pair whose cfg names a SPECIFICATION, invariant, or constant the module does not declare are both errors -- "I could not measure this" -- never a silent bound = None. Two test fixtures (tests/test_new_ticket_workflow.py, tests/test_skill_feedback.py) and one spec-unit adapter fixture (specs/current/production_adapters.py) were passing exactly that shape through the ledger and had to become real models; that is the fix finding its own blast radius, not collateral. CM-F2: per-module action scope took Scenario_RejectedRequests from 7 wrong zero-case warnings to 0, with an identical 14-case corpus (results/cm-f2-action-scope.txt). The probe reproduces: 160 / 16 / 14 and 732 for the whole view (results/case_module_coverage.txt). The aggregation report gates nothing and exits 0 on uncovered actions. Two findings deferred: CM-01-DF-01 (the pre-existing red doc-phrase test) and CM-01-DF-02 (parse_cfg_invariants returns the keyword line that terminates an INVARIANT block, which forced a CFG_KEYWORDS workaround in the new validator).

refinement.detail: Searched for a representation that would let the coverage report be derived rather than declared -- i.e. recover a case module's action scope from the module's own next-state relation instead of from spec_manifest.yaml. It is recoverable statically (analyze_complexity.extract_next_actions already does it), but it would silently agree with whatever the module happens to do, which is the opposite of what a declaration is for: the value of the block is that a stale scope is VISIBLE as drift. Nothing was applied. The one real reduction available -- deleting the R4-DF-04 warning rather than scoping it -- would have removed a true finding to silence a false one.

ticket.model_delta_expectation: ZERO. Case-module generation lives in generate_cases_from_tlc_dump.py, which the CLI lifecycle model does not represent. Document the no-op model result with evidence at close; do not invent an action to have a delta.
ticket.objective: Mechanize the case-module option and fix the defect the probe found underneath it. Three parts, in this order. (1) CM-F1 -- record_complexity_ledger locates its model as the alphabetically first *.tla excluding MC*, which on any Core/Internal/External baseline resolves to Core.tla paired with External.cfg and measures bound=None, modularity=0.0; the standing-objective ledger has been measuring a module with no variables and no actions. The measured model becomes DECLARED, and a mismatched .tla/.cfg pair is an error rather than a silent measurement. This is a live defect on every three-module project, independent of case modules. (2) A `case_modules:` block in spec_manifest.yaml -- per module, the view it extends, its action subset, and (for a Given form) the recorded claim the Given asserts. (3) Per-module action scope so generation stops emitting the R4-DF-04 zero-case alias-wrapper warning for actions that simply are not in this aspect (CM-F2), plus an aggregation report of per-action coverage across modules against the view's action set -- a report, never a gate.
ticket.title: Case modules: declared model discovery, manifest block, per-module action scope, corpus aggregation
